body_markdown:
The second-generation Porsche Macan released for 2025 was developed exclusively with electric power in mind. That was a risky bet; it’s one of the brand’s best-selling models, and the EV hasn’t fully lived up to expectations. Porsche confirmed[a long-standing rumor](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/porsche-revises-ev-ambitions-with-ice-macan-considered/) by announcing that a gasoline-burning follow-up to[the first-generation Macan](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2020-porsche-macan-gets-the-gts-treatment/) will go on sale before the end of the decade.


“We have to be careful to ensure that the company was not making a double investment in petrol and EVs in the same vehicle segment. We have to recover our petrol strategy, but I’m very positive that once we have the Macan with the petrol engine, we have a very balanced offer for our customers on electric and petrol cars,” said Porsche CEO Michael Leiters, according to *[AutoGuide](https://www.autoguide.com/auto/porsche-revives-gas-macan-for-2028-keeps-911-petrol-44639689)* .


The publication added that sales of the electric Macan fell by about 40% in the first half of 2026 compared to the first half of 2025.

What the next gasoline-powered Macan will look like remains to be seen. It’s unlikely to land as merely an evolution of[the current model](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2026-porsche-macan-gts-specs-suspension-pictures/) (pictured) with a V-6 instead of electric motors, because the EV is built on the Premium Platform Electric (PPE) architecture that was designed exclusively for battery-powered models. It’s also found under[the Audi A6 E-Tron](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/audis-a6-e-tron-is-a-slippery-people-hauling-ev/) , among other electric cars.


Similarly, specifications aren’t available. We’re expecting four- and six-cylinder engines paired with all-wheel-drive, and a hybrid model could be part of the range. Porsche will likely offer several variants of the ICE-powered Macan, including a Turbo and a GTS.


More information about the next ICE-powered Porsche Macan will emerge in the coming months. It’s tentatively due out in 2028, which suggests that it could land on dealer lots as a 2029 model. And nothing suggests that it will replace the EV. Porsche will simultaneously sell both variants and let buyers choose the one that suits them best. BMW is taking a similar approach to EVs: The new 3 Series is available[with a wide variety of gasoline-burning engines](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/the-2027-bmw-3-series-were-most-excited-to-drive-isnt-the-ev-or-the-m3/) and as an electric model[that resurrects the i3 nameplate](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2027-bmw-i3-3-series-specs-pictures-performance/) .


## What About Sports Cars?


Porsche isn’t giving up on EVs; far from it. It’s simply responding to a market that’s not leaning as heavily towards EVs as many predicted. Leiters confirmed that work on several electric models continues, including the replacements for the 718 Cayman and the 718 Boxster. Unverified reports[claim](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/report-porsche-pulls-another-u-turn-as-next-cayman-and-boxster-to-get-gas-engines/) that they’ll also be available with battery and gasoline power, though nothing is official.


Making the 911 electric is still out of the question, according to the executive. Even a plug-in hybrid model has been ruled out, because the drivetrain’s additional hardware would make the car bigger. Buyers who want an electrified 911 aren’t entirely out of luck, however:[The Carrera GTS](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2025-porsche-911-carrera-gts-review-e-gads/) is fitted with Porsche’s T-Hybrid system, which stuffs an electric motor in the transmission.
